title: ISTH DIC Score
keywords: only apply this score if the patient has an underlying disorder known to be associated with DIC, sepsis, trauma, malignancy, obstetric catastrophe, it is not a general coagulopathy screen
score of 5 or more is compatible with overt DIC
score under 5 is suggestive but not confirmatory of non-overt DIC, repeat in 1-2 days if clinical suspicion persists
2025 ISTH update quantified the D-dimer thresholds at greater than 3 times and greater than 7 times the upper limit of normal for the 2 and 3 point tiers
sources: Taylor FB, et al. Towards definition, clinical and laboratory criteria, and a scoring system for disseminated intravascular coagulation. Thromb Haemost. 2001;86(5):1327-1330.
ISTH SSC Subcommittee on DIC. Updated definition and scoring of disseminated intravascular coagulation in 2025. J Thromb Haemost. 2025.

changelog.change: Initial entry — a genuine content gap (Content audit 2026-09-15, fresh-look Batch 6). DIC was referenced across roughly 10 existing modules (transfusion reactions, postpartum hemorrhage, heat stroke, sepsis-related content) with no scoring tool anywhere in the corpus. D-dimer point thresholds reflect the ISTH 2025 update quantifying what were previously the more subjective 'moderate vs strong increase' categories.

purpose: Quantifies overt disseminated intravascular coagulation in a patient with a KNOWN underlying disorder associated with DIC (sepsis, trauma, malignancy, obstetric catastrophe, etc.) — this is not a general coagulopathy screening tool for an undifferentiated patient.
notes: Apply only when there is a clinical suspicion of DIC in the context of an associated underlying condition. A score under 5 does not exclude non-overt/early-phase DIC — if suspicion remains, repeat the panel in 1-2 days.

options.label: Moderate increase (> 3× upper limit of normal)
Strong increase (> 7× upper limit of normal)

items.label: Prothrombin time prolongation (seconds above upper limit of normal)

interpretation.label: Not compatible with overt DIC
interpretation.detail: Suggestive of non-overt (early-phase/pre-DIC) or no DIC. If clinical suspicion persists given the underlying condition, repeat the panel in 1-2 days rather than excluding DIC on a single low score.

interpretation.label: Compatible with overt DIC
interpretation.detail: Treat the underlying cause aggressively, provide hemostatic support (platelets, FFP, cryoprecipitate) guided by bleeding and lab trends, and consider anticoagulation only in select cases per hematology input.
interpretation.disposition: Hematology involvement; treat underlying trigger; hemostatic support guided by bleeding/labs

buildNote: Point structure and the 5-point overt-DIC threshold WebSearch-verified against the original Taylor et al. 2001 ISTH criteria and the 2025 ISTH SSC update, which quantified the D-dimer moderate/strong increase thresholds at >3x and >7x ULN respectively (previously more subjectively defined). Deliberately framed in purpose/notes as applicable only with a known DIC-associated underlying condition, matching the original ISTH algorithm's first step (which this tool does not itself score, since it's a yes/no clinical gate rather than a point-scored item).
